providers.description: A single authoritative oracle for real-time on-chain and market intelligence: crypto prices, market cap and volume, DeFi TVL, fiat exchange rates, network gas prices, wallet balances and transaction lookups across Ethereum and Base. Every answer is number-first, canonical and independently reproducible — sourced from professional public feeds (CoinGecko, DefiLlama, public RPC, exchange-rate feeds) and recorded on Telegraph as a hashed, verifiable signal. A heuristic read over a token's recent ERC-20 Transfer logs, scanned live over public RPC. It is a signal, not a proof of intent: it measures the patterns wash trading leaves behind. Reciprocal address pairs where value goes out and comes back, self-transfers, plus volume concentrated in a few senders all raise a bounded risk score the answer labels low, elevated or high. The block window is bounded and the node's log range is shrunk when it reports too many results, so a busy token can never exhaust the worker. Reads on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism and Polygon. Answers the WASH_TRADING_DETECTION intent. No API key, nothing cached that can go stale.

blocks.description: Scan window in blocks, defaults to 120, capped at 600.

chain.description: Chain to read on, one of ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon.

question.description: The full natural-language question, verbatim, for example "Does token 0xabc... show wash-trading patterns on Ethereum?". The miner reads the token and the chain from it, so passing the whole question works as well as the fields.

token.description: Token address or symbol whose Transfer logs to scan.

reciprocal_pairs.description: Address pairs that sent value both ways in the window.

risk_score.description: A bounded 0 to 1 blend of the measured signals.

summary.description: One sentence with the risk verdict and the key figures.

transfers.description: How many Transfer logs were analyzed.

verified.description: True when the risk label is LOW.

input.description: Intent-specific structured input. For URL_SAFE, provide url; for THREAT_IP_REPUTATION, provide ip or ip_address; for THREAT_INTELLIGENCE, provide indicator and optional indicator_type; for PLAGIARISM_DETECTION, provide text and comparison_documents; for SECURITY_REVIEW, provide code or configuration; for REGRESSION_VERIFY, provide base_url and checks against an allowlisted HTTPS host; for CODE_PATCH_VERIFY, provide repository in owner/repo format and commit_sha; for VULNERABILITY_TRIAGE, provide findings with CVSS/severity, exploitation status, and asset context.

intent.description: The canonical Telegraph Intent handled by the response.

retrieved_at.description: Timestamp indicating when information was retrieved or generated.

uncertainty.description: Known uncertainty or limitations associated with the response.

verdict.description: Primary decision or classification produced by the handler.

Reads the latest on-chain ETH balance of an Ethereum mainnet address from the Ethplorer API and returns a small JSON answer (under 1 KB) with ETH.balance in decimal ETH and ETH.rawBalance in wei. Serves ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY questions anchored at "latest" about an address's native ETH balance. Current state only - Ethplorer has no historical-block parameter, so a block_number in the request is accepted but the value returned is always the latest balance.

token.description: Constant token filter that suppresses the token list.

ETH.description: balance (number, ETH units), rawBalance (string, wei) and price (USD market data, not the answer).

address.description: Lower-cased echo of the queried address.

contractInfo.description: Non-empty only when the address is a contract.

providers.description: A specific value read from a blockchain node at a stated block height or latest, which is what marks this intent apart from a plain lookup. Serves a raw contract view call, a storage slot, a token balance held by an address, plus a transaction's gas used with its first Transfer log amount, each anchored to the block it was read at. Read over public RPC on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism and Polygon. Answers the ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY intent. No API key, nothing cached that can go stale.

block.description: Block height or the word latest. Defaults to latest.

chain.description: Chain to read on, one of ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon.

hash.description: Transaction hash for a gas-used and Transfer-log read.

holder.description: Address whose token balance to read.

question.description: The full natural-language question, verbatim, for example "At block 21000000 on Ethereum, how much gas did tx 0xabc... use?". The miner reads the metric and the block anchor from it, so passing the whole question works as well as the fields.

slot.description: Storage slot for a storage read, with the contract in address.

to.description: Contract address for a view call.

token.description: Token address or symbol for a balance read.

block.description: The block anchor the value was read at.

confidence.description: 0.97 to 0.98 for a direct on-chain read.

metric.description: Which metric was read, one of view_call, storage, token_balance, gas_used.

summary.description: One sentence naming the value and the block it was read at.

value.description: The raw value read, when the metric is a call or a storage slot.

value_uint.description: The value decoded as an unsigned integer, when it is a 32-byte word.

Bid-ask spread, book depth and the slippage a stated trade size would incur for a named market. A crypto pair is walked on the Kraken public order book, so the spread, the depth within two percent of mid and the average fill price are live reads. When a chain is named the WETH/USDC style pool is quoted on the Uniswap v3 QuoterV2 contract over public RPC, so the slippage is the pool's own answer. Answers the LIQUIDITY_DEPTH_VERIFY intent. No API key, nothing cached that can go stale.

chain.description: Chain for an on-chain pool quote, for example base. Omit for a centralized book.

pair.description: Market or pair, for example BTC/USD or WETH/USDC.

question.description: The full natural-language question, verbatim, for example "What is the bid-ask spread and slippage on a 50 ETH sell into the WETH/USDC pool on Base?". The miner reads the pair, size and any chain from it, so passing the whole question works as well as the structured fields.

size.description: Trade size in the base asset, for the slippage estimate.

confidence.description: 0.96 for a book quote, 0.95 for an on-chain pool quote.

market_type.description: central limit order book or on-chain AMM pool.

mid_price.description: Mid price for a book quote.

pair.description: The market the answer is for.

slippage_percent.description: Slippage of the stated size against mid or spot, as a percentage.

spread.description: Ask minus bid for a book quote.

spread_bps.description: Spread in basis points of the mid.

summary.description: One sentence with the spread, the depth and the slippage for the size.

trade_size.description: The trade size the slippage is for.

venue.description: Kraken for a book, Uniswap v3 for an on-chain pool.

acceptanceBeforeAnotherReview: Confirm Engine routing to providers that answer the exact requested token and chain.
Resolve the recorded paid liquidity failure and audit routing failure with the upstream operator.
Confirm a supported Intent/schema for contract state at an explicit block.
Confirm executable USD depth for the exact token, chain and notional, including route/fee/slippage constraints; reserve value is insufficient.
Do not treat a catalogue entry, advertised schema or empty leaderboard as proof that a provider succeeds or fails.
